title: Rewrite examples
description:
I got suggestions back from CRAN for my initial submission:

```
Thanks,

If there are references describing the methods in your package, please add these in the description field of your DESCRIPTION file in the form authors (year) <doi:...> authors (year, ISBN:...) or if those are not available: <https:...> with no space after 'doi:', 'https:' and angle brackets for auto-linking. (If you want to add a title as well please put it in
quotes: "Title")
For more details: 
<https://contributor.r-project.org/cran-cookbook/description_issues.html#references>

\dontrun{} should only be used if the example really cannot be executed (e.g. because of missing additional software, missing API keys, ...) by the user. That's why wrapping examples in \dontrun{} adds the comment ("# Not run:") as a warning for the user. Does not seem necessary. 
Please replace \dontrun with \donttest.

Please unwrap the examples if they are executable in < 5 sec, or replace dontrun{} with \donttest{}.

Please replace the \dontrun{}-wrapper with if(interactive()){} for interactive examples.

For more details: 
<https://contributor.r-project.org/cran-cookbook/general_issues.html#structuring-of-examples> 


Please ensure that your functions do not write by default or in your examples/vignettes/tests in the user's home filespace (including the package directory and getwd()). This is not allowed by CRAN policies. 
Please omit any default path in writing functions. In your examples/vignettes/tests you can write to tempdir().
For more details: 
<https://contributor.r-project.org/cran-cookbook/code_issues.html#writing-files-and-directories-to-the-home-filespace>

Please fix and resubmit.

Best,
Konstanze Lauseker (she/her)
```

I have already responded to the first point in `cran-commends.md`.

The task now for us it to tackle the last points.

Can you please:

1) in snapshot(), omit any default path(?) and warn the users that we will be writing snapshot files to the designated directory.
2) To make CRAN happy with examples, I think we need a new helper function called `with_example` or sth that makes more sense (you decide whether we make this function public or private), which creates an example project in tempdir() and temporarily sets the working directory there.
3) The example should contain:
    a) a _resultcheck.yml to make find_root() work
    b) a simple `analysis.R` script that has sth like:
        ```r
        model <- lm(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars)
        resultcheck::snapshot(model, "model")
        ```
    c) the corresponding snapshot files, maybe one copy for the actual correct snapshot, one slightly tweaked (e.g. change 37.29 to 38.29) to let the user have an example (in snapshot()) of how it looks like when things go wrong (in interactive mode only, with if(interactive()){}).
    d) a testthat test that looks sth like:
    ```r
    library(testthat)
    library(resultcheck)
    
    test_that("run_tested_script", {
        sandbox <- setup_sandbox("resultcheck-test.R")
        on.exit(cleanup_sandbox(sandbox), add = TRUE)
    
        run_in_sandbox("resultcheck-test.R", sandbox = sandbox)
    
        expect_equal(1, 1)
    })
    ```
    
        You see there's an additional problem that we need `expect_equal(1, 1)` to prevent the test from being skipped. Can you find a way to let run_in_sandbox() emit a result that is "passed" by testthat?
4) Maybe the example I gave you is not in the ideal (maybe the sandbox creation/destruction should be inside/outside test_that? I don't know). Just make sure the docs are consistent among themselves, and with the examples we create.
5) With everything above, we can update the examples and vignettes to make CRAN happy. In this case, I think we no longer need \dontrun or \donttest, but one instance of if(interactive()) for the failure example in snapshot()

Is everything clear? Or did I make any mistake?

title: Option to choose print only or str only snapshot
description:

However, in some cases, one method might not be suited for snapshotting. For example:

title: Create location and snapshot functions
description:
At this point we are ready for some new functions. I think what would be exceptionally useful is interactive snapshotting, which would be useful for empirical researchers who are not used to store their objects into .rds or .rdata files and want to be notified of changes when they are doing interactive analysis. In `testthat` we have https://testthat.r-lib.org/articles/snapshotting.html, but it doesn't allow for interactive uses.

I would like this scenario:
1. The user writes code in a .R script for analysis.
2. Once she produces a plot/table/regression, etc objects, she can, in the following line, invoke the snapshot function. For the first time this would only save the snapshot into a .md file, like what `testthat` does. But for subsequent executions, he/she will be notified if there are any differences in the new outputs and be prompted to update the snapshots.
3. Automatic tests (those run by testthat in sandboxes) can utilize the snapshots for comparisons.

I really like how `testthat` produces human-readable snapshots. maybe we can borrow/copy their snapshotting? Their repo: https://github.com/r-lib/testthat/

But this would mean that we need to decide on where to put our test results. Ideally, they should be in a subdirectory of the project. But R users are notoriously bad for wd management. I think maybe we can leverage rprojroot with sth like:
```{r}
root <- rprojroot::find_root(
  rprojroot::has_file("resultcheck.yml"),
  rprojroot::has_file(".Rproj"),
  rprojroot::has_dir(".git")
)
```

where `resultcheck.yml` is our placeholder for the config file for our package, where users can put custom setting information in. This way, we don't rely on the user to set wd directly. Not that I haven't add requirement for rprojroot in DESCRIPTION now.

Another thing is that we need to decide on how to *name* the snapshot files. This can be annoying. Because the name has to be specified in the snapshot function (otherwise we won't be able to find it). Also, should we keep them under a subdirectory named after the script file name? IDK what's the best practice? what's done in testthat?

Another thing is that, maybe our sandboxing should add an option to automatically copy the relevant snapshots even the user doesn't specify their locations. This should be defaulted to TRUE unless the user opt out of it. Does that make sense? We can easily tell which snapshot files are relevant by screening through the code, or is that too dangerous a thing to do?

Feel free to discuss with me if anything is unclear/unsure.
